evan: FYI rolled AWQ quantized weights to canary on prod-dedicated last night. Started seeing OOMs on 8xA100 during long multi-turn chat (~1k tokens). nvprof shows big transient allocations during matmul/dequant paths.
maya: ouch. any quick numbers? peak mem before/after?
ev an: before: ~28.4GB steady. after deploy peak hit 39.2GB and then OOMed. steady working set still ~26GB but spikes during generation (~12-15k tensors allocated briefly).
raj: spike sounds like dequant -> fp16/32 temp buffers. AWQ keeps int8 on disk but we dequantize to fp16 for kernels unless we have int8-compatible kernels. are we forcing dequant into fp32 anywhere?
ev an: our runtime path had a fallback for gemm that dequantizes to fp32 for cublasLT path. code snippet from runtime logs:
``
if (!int8_fast_path) {
  weights = dequantize(weights, dtype=torch.float32);
  cublas_gemm(..., dtype=float32)
}
```
maya: that explains memory spike. GPUs allocate big workspaces for fp32 matmuls. can we switch fallback to fp16 cublasLt or use mixed-precision kernels?
zara: also saw KV cache dtype was float32 in canary config (legacy). KV for 1k tokens + batch=2 eats RAM. set KV dtype=float16 reduces cache by ~2x.
loren: quick mitigation options:
- force KV cache dtype=float16
- enable in-place dequant or lazy dequant (keep int8 and dequantize tile-by-tile)
- PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF tuning
- reduce max workspace size for cublasLt
we should try them in order.
raj: agreed. i tested lazy dequant pattern locally — peak down from 36GB -> 27GB. looked like we were creating full fp32 copy before kernel instead of streaming tiles.
ev an: any patches to runtime to reuse dequant buffer across steps?
maya: pushed a tiny PR that reuses a preallocated workspace for dequant and GEMM scratch. patch uses a per-device workspace allocator with behaviour:
- allocate once at model load: workspace_max = min(gpu_mem*0.15, 16GB)
- sub-allocate for dequant/kernels
- reclaim on model unload
perf locally: peak 28.6GB -> 24.9GB for long chat length 1500 tokens (batch=2).
zara: nice. did you set PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF? we got fragmentation on A100s until we set `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128,garbage_collection_threshold:0.6` which reduced fragmentation and transient peak by ~1.2GB.
loren: another lever: batching heuristics. our dynamic batcher was allowing a big batch to coalesce (batch 8) during opensessions which multiplied KV usage. set batching upper bound to 4 for canary to keep steady GPU footprint while we tune.
ev an: did end-to-end profiling with nsys (nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt -o awq_canary) — found hotspots:
- cublasLt matmul (fp32 fallback) 42% of time, big workspace allocs
- dequant kernel 18%
- kv_cache write 12%
attached quick summary: peak mem 39.2GB, after allocator+kv=float16+batch=4 -> peak 26.3GB, throughput drop 8%.
raj: 8% throughput trade for avoiding OOM is fine w/ SLOs. but need longer run: do a 24h soak. also test edge cases: long context skew and multi-turn little tokens but many requests.
maya: watch out for mixed-precision pitfalls: some MHA kernels expect bfloat16 vs float16; quantized weight reorder may not be compatible. add a model-compatibility check during model import to pick safest dtype and kernel set.
zara: for Dedicated customers we should expose KV dtype toggle in Console (small toggle) + warning about perf/cost.

4) follow-up: upstream upstream kernels for int8 gemm (invest in int8-friendly cublasLt or fused kernels) — long term
